# aarch64-study

> AArch64 SoC simulator that runs in the browser. Rust → WebAssembly core,
> React UI. Each released version adds exactly one architectural concept.
> Reading the diff between two tags is the lesson.

Live demo: <https://labs.golia.jp/aarch64/>
License: MIT

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md) — entry point (English)
- [README.zh.md](README.zh.md) — 简体中文
- [README.ja.md](README.ja.md) — 日本語
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) — version-by-version concept history

## Source layout

- `crates/aarch64-sim/src/lib.rs` — entire CPU + MMU + AIC + Block + demo
  program + tests in one Rust file. Pure-Rust API.
- `crates/aarch64-sim/src/wasm.rs` — `#[wasm_bindgen]` wrappers, gated by
  `feature = "wasm"`; the JS surface (`cpu.step()`, `cpu.state()`, …) lives
  here.
- `crates/aarch64-sim/src/bin/cli.rs` — `aarch64-sim` CLI (clap derive),
  gated by `feature = "cli"`. Subcommands: `run`, `disasm`, `mem`.
- `crates/aarch64-sim/examples/` — pure-Rust embed (`run.rs`,
  `disassemble.rs`) and a single-page WASM demo (`wasm-web/`).
- `src/views/cpu.tsx` — top-level page. Boots the simulator, runs the
  refresh loop, drives auto-run, composes panels.
- `src/components/system-diagram.tsx` — SoC pin-out SVG schematic.
- `src/components/panels/*` — one file per panel (AIC, Block, Memory,
  MMU, Output, Save, Disassembly, CoreMonitor).
- `src/components/{badges,control-bar,reg-row}.tsx` — shared UI.
- `src/sim/types.ts` — wasm-bindgen mirror types.
- `src/sim/format.ts` — formatters, parsers, demo constants.
- `src/sim/events.ts` — pure SimEvent derivation from snapshot diff.

## Build & test

```
bun install            # also: rm -rf node_modules/aarch64-sim if WASM was rebuilt
bun run build:sim      # wasm-pack the Rust simulator
bun run dev            # vite dev server on :32030
bun run test:sim       # cargo test (24 tests)
bun run check          # tsc + eslint + prettier
bun run build          # production bundle into ./dist
bun run deploy         # build + rsync dist/ to the production target

# crate-side
cargo build -p aarch64-sim                   # pure-Rust lib
cargo build -p aarch64-sim --features cli    # build the aarch64-sim CLI
cargo run -p aarch64-sim --example run       # pure-Rust embed example
cargo publish -p aarch64-sim --dry-run       # verify before releasing
```

`bun run build:sim` invokes wasm-pack with `-- --features wasm`. After
`build:sim`, run `rm -rf node_modules/aarch64-sim && bun install` before
`bun run build` so Vite picks up the regenerated WASM.

## Conventions

- GDS theme tokens only (`bg-surface`, `text-fg`, `palette-X`, …); avoid
  hand-picked colour shades so light + dark both render cleanly.
- Roboto Mono for any numeric / hex / register column (via `mono-data`);
  Roboto Flex for plain UI text with `tabular-nums`.
- Animations depict real simulator events. No ambient sci-fi.
- Tasks pinned per core: core 0 = task A (LDXR/STXR atomic counter at
  PA 0x6FF8, then SVC #0 to ask the kernel to ping core 1, then WFI),
  core 1 = task B (disk printer, parks in WFI after one pass). Auto-run
  pauses once every core is halted or parked in WFI; pressing Run again
  auto-resets.
